Join Stryker's Joint Replacement division as a 
Senior Modeling and Simulation Engineer, R&D - NPD
. This 
hybrid role is based in Mahwah, New Jersey
, with an expectation of working onsite three days per week and the flexibility to work remotely on other days. Candidates must live within commuting distance of the Mahwah office.
At Stryker, we’re transforming orthopaedic innovation through cutting-edge modeling and simulation technologies. As a Senior Engineer on our Joint Replacement team, you’ll help shape the future of implant design and robotic procedures driving meaningful impact for patients and surgeons worldwide. If you're energized by discovery-based research and thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced environment, this is your opportunity to make a difference.
To learn more about Stryker’s Joint Replacement portfolio visit: 
Joint Replacement
What You Will Do
Conduct comprehensive literature reviews to inform analytical methods and assumptions.
Execute advanced finite element analyses, including nonlinear multibody simulations with deformable contact and multi-physics.
Develop and automate simulation techniques using custom programming tools.
Train machine learning algorithms using simulation data to generate more efficient predictive models.
Analyze simulation results and recommend design, material, or process improvements.
Build and validate analytical models to support research and development initiatives.
Collect and integrate physical testing, manufacturing, and clinical data to enhance model accuracy.
Author technical reports for regulatory submissions and publish findings in peer-reviewed journals and industry conferences.
Collaborate cross-functionally to develop next-generation orthopaedic technologies and devices.
What You Need
Required
Bachelor’s degree in a science or engineering discipline.
Minimum 2 years of engineering experience.
Experience in modeling and simulation-based research.
Preferred
Master’s or PhD in Mechanical or Biomedical Engineering.
Experience in the medical device industry.
Proficiency with FEA tools (e.g., ANSYS, Abaqus, LS-Dyna, Hyperworks), CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks, Pro/Engineer), and programming languages (e.g., Matlab, Python, Fortran).
Familiarity with musculoskeletal simulation platforms (e.g., OpenSim).
Demonstrated ability to contribute to complex research initiatives from concept to recommendation.
Knowledge of mechanics, engineering principles, and product development processes.

EXP-003 A/B/D/F/G/H: numerical solvers, XFEM, nonlinear material models, reduced-order methods, experimental calibration and research software.

qualification_matches.requirement: Advanced FEA, nonlinear multibody/deformable contact and multiphysics
qualification_matches.evidence: EXP-003 A/B supports multiphysics and nonlinear constitutive models; EXP-001 N/O/Q supports assembly/material/impact FEA. Full nonlinear multibody deformable-contact workflow is not established.
EXP-001 A/D Python/CadQuery and numerical workflows; EXP-002 C C/C++ simulation.
EXP-003 G: neural-network damage surrogate trained on high-fidelity XFEM simulations. Does not establish medical-device ML deployment.
EXP-003 F measured modal response and structural model updating; EXP-001 E/F/J prototype experiments and Q/R impact analysis/testing.

qualification_matches.evidence: Python and C/C++ evidenced in achievements. Inventory mentions some commercial products but professional use of ANSYS/Abaqus/SolidWorks is not independently established; LS-Dyna, Hyperworks, Pro/Engineer, Fortran and OpenSim not established.
